**Derivation.** Rewrite the system as
$$a=\frac{by}{z}+\frac{cz}{y},\qquad b=\frac{cz}{x}+\frac{ax}{z},\qquad c=\frac{ax}{y}+\frac{by}{x}.$$
Set $x=1$ (the equations are scale-invariant in $x,y,z$) and take $z=1$, $y=\omega$ where $\omega=e^{i\pi/3}$ (so $\omega^2-\omega+1=0$ and $\omega+\omega^{-1}=1$). The system becomes
$$a=b\omega+\frac{c}{\omega},\qquad b=c+a,\qquad c=a\omega+\frac{b}{\omega}.$$
From $b=c+a$ we get $c=a(1-\omega)$ and $b=a(2-\omega)$. Substituting into the first and third equations confirms consistency (using $\omega^{-1}=1-\omega$).

Now $abc=a^3(2-\omega)(1-\omega)=a^3(1-2\omega)=1$, so $a^3=\frac1{1-2\omega}$. Compute
$$(2-\omega)^3=3-6\omega,\qquad (1-\omega)^3=-1,$$
hence
$$a^3+b^3+c^3=a^3\bigl[1+(2-\omega)^3+(1-\omega)^3\bigr]=a^3(3-6\omega)=\frac{3-6\omega}{1-2\omega}=3.$$
Since $abc=1$, this equals $3abc$, and the value is independent of the particular solution branch.
